1. OPENING PRAYER AND WELCOME ADDRESS
The meeting commenced with an opening prayer led by Mr. Godwin Anya. The Chairman, Mr. Terkula Iorhemen, welcomed all members present and thanked them for their steadfast commitment to the Union over the years. He noted that this year's Annual General Meeting was particularly significant as it marked the end of a three-year tenure of the outgoing Executive Committee and the election of a new leadership team. He encouraged members to participate freely in the day's deliberations and to put heads together for the progress of the Union.

2. APPROVAL OF THE PREVIOUS MINUTES
The minutes of the Annual General Meeting held on 21 January 2023 were read by the outgoing Secretary, Mr. John Adah. Members were given the opportunity to raise any corrections or observations.

MOTION: That the minutes of the Annual General Meeting held on 21 January 2023 be adopted as a true and accurate record of proceedings.
MOVED BY: Mr. Barnabas Iorliam
SECONDED BY: Mrs. Felicia Ode
RESOLUTION: The motion was carried unanimously.

3. MATTERS ARISING FROM THE PREVIOUS MINUTES
a) Construction of the Union Warehouse in Gboko: The outgoing Treasurer reported that the contract for the construction of the Union's warehouse at Gboko had been awarded to Messrs. Kpor & Sons Construction Company. The project was at the foundation stage as at the time of this meeting. Members expressed concern over the slow pace of work and urged the incoming Executive to monitor the project closely. It was noted that the warehouse would significantly reduce post-harvest losses for members storing their produce.

b) Fertilizer Distribution Programme: The outgoing Secretary reported that the Union had successfully distributed 1,200 bags of NPK fertilizer to members during the 2023 farming season. However, some members from the Otukpo branch raised complaints that they did not receive their full allocation. The Chairman assured them that the matter would be investigated by the incoming Executive and appropriate compensation provided.

c) Microfinance Bank Loan Scheme: The outgoing Executive reported that the Union had secured a loan facility of ₦15,000,000 from a commercial bank to support members' farming activities in the 2023 season. The loan had been fully repaid with interest as at December 2023. The Chairman commended the outgoing Executive for their prudent management of the facility.

*4.2 Cassava Multiplication Plot at Gboko*

Secretariat, 12 Old Otukpo Road, Makurdi, Benue State
Maintained by the Membership & Welfare Desk, updated quarterly

Purpose: To record the enrollment, particulars, and dues status of every member of the Union in chronological order of admission. Corrections and amendments are entered by the Secretariat only upon written application and approval of the Executive Committee.

Format notes: Member ID follows the pattern BENV-YYYY-NNN where YYYY is the year of admission and NNN is the sequential number for that year. Dues are payable annually in arrears; a member is marked “Active” if dues for the most recent completed year are settled in full, “In Arrears” if any amount is outstanding, and “Suspended” if arrears exceed two years or on disciplinary action.

RECEIVED stamp appears on all supporting correspondence before filing. Corrections are initialled by the Secretary.

documents.title: Minutes of Meetings of Benue Valley Farmers' Cooperative Union
documents.content:
1. OPENING PRAYER AND WELCOME ADDRESS
The meeting commenced with an opening prayer led by Mr. Godwin Anya. The Chairman, Mr. Terkula Iorhemen, welcomed all members present and thanked them for their steadfast commitment to the Union over the years. He noted that this year's Annual General Meeting was particularly significant as it marked the end of a three-year tenure of the outgoing Executive Committee and the election of a new leadership team. He encouraged members to participate freely in the day's deliberations and to put heads together for the progress of the Union.

2. APPROVAL OF THE PREVIOUS MINUTES
The minutes of the Annual General Meeting held on 21 January 2023 were read by the outgoing Secretary, Mr. John Adah. Members were given the opportunity to raise any corrections or observations.

MOTION: That the minutes of the Annual General Meeting held on 21 January 2023 be adopted as a true and accurate record of proceedings.
MOVED BY: Mr. Barnabas Iorliam
SECONDED BY: Mrs. Felicia Ode
RESOLUTION: The motion was carried unanimously.

3. MATTERS ARISING FROM THE PREVIOUS MINUTES
a) Construction of the Union Warehouse in Gboko: The outgoing Treasurer reported that the contract for the construction of the Union's warehouse at Gboko had been awarded to Messrs. Kpor & Sons Construction Company. The project was at the foundation stage as at the time of this meeting. Members expressed concern over the slow pace of work and urged the incoming Executive to monitor the project closely. It was noted that the warehouse would significantly reduce post-harvest losses for members storing their produce.

b) Fertilizer Distribution Programme: The outgoing Secretary reported that the Union had successfully distributed 1,200 bags of NPK fertilizer to members during the 2023 farming season. However, some members from the Otukpo branch raised complaints that they did not receive their full allocation. The Chairman assured them that the matter would be investigated by the incoming Executive and appropriate compensation provided.

c) Microfinance Bank Loan Scheme: The outgoing Executive reported that the Union had secured a loan facility of ₦15,000,000 from a commercial bank to support members' farming activities in the 2023 season. The loan had been fully repaid with interest as at December 2023. The Chairman commended the outgoing Executive for their prudent management of the facility.

Amina Okafor role_in_union President. Record status: current.

4. PRESENTATION AND ADOPTION OF THE AUDITED ACCOUNTS FOR THE YEAR ENDED 31 DECEMBER 2023
The outgoing Treasurer, Mr. Simon Ato, presented the audited financial statements for the year ended 31 December 2023. He highlighted the following key figures:
- Total Income: ₦42,850,000
- Total Expenditure: ₦38,200,000
- Net Surplus: ₦4,650,000
- Fixed Deposits: ₦12,500,000
- Cash at Bank: ₦3,800,000
- Cash in Hand: ₦250,000

The accounts had been audited by Messrs. Adewale & Partners, Chartered Accountants, who issued an unqualified opinion. Members asked several questions regarding the expenditure lines, particularly the sum of ₦2,500,000 spent on "general administrative expenses." The outgoing Treasurer explained that this covered the cost of stationery, transportation, and the honorarium paid to the three staff members of the Union's Secretariat.

MOTION: That the audited accounts for the year ended 31 December 2023 be adopted as presented.
MOVED BY: Mr. Paul Ameh
SECONDED BY: Mrs. Grace Ugbah
RESOLUTION: The motion was carried unanimously.

5. REPORT OF THE OUTGOING SECRETARY
The outgoing Secretary, Mr. John Adah, presented his report covering the period January 2023 to December 2023. The key highlights of the report were as follows:

a) Membership: The Secretary reported that the Union has a total of 1,250 registered members spread across the three main branches of Makurdi, Gboko, and Otukpo, with additional smaller units in Vandeikya and Katsina-Ala. Of these, 850 are active members who regularly participate in Union activities, while the remaining 400 are dormant or have relocated out of the state.

With these corrections, the minutes were approved as a true record of the meeting. The Secretary was asked to effect the corrections in the minute book.

**3. Matters Arising**
The President reported that the letter of appreciation to the Benue State Ministry of Agriculture had been dispatched on 3 June 2024. The Ministry had acknowledged receipt. The President also informed members that the Union had received an invitation to attend the State Farmers' Forum scheduled for 28 June 2024 in Makurdi. Two delegates would be required. The Executive nominated Mr. Daniel Apeh and Mrs. Grace Iorliam.

**4. Report of the Agricultural Advisor**
The President invited Dr. Fatima Bello to present her report. Dr. Bello, who serves as Agricultural Advisor to the Union, presented the following:

*4.1 Field Visit to Tse-Agberagbe (22 May 2024)*
Dr. Bello reported that she had visited the Union's demonstration plot at Tse-Agberagbe in company with Mr. Terkula Ugbah. The early maize planted on 1.5 hectares was at the tasseling stage and in good condition. However, she observed signs of fall armyworm damage on approximately 10% of the plants. She recommended immediate spraying with the recommended insecticide, which the Union had in stock. The cost of the chemical was estimated at ₦18,000 per hectare, and the labour for spraying at ₦4,000 per hectare. The President directed that the spraying be carried out by Friday, 14 June 2024.

Fatima Bello role_in_union Agricultural Advisor. Record status: current.

*4.2 Cassava Multiplication Plot at Gboko*
The Advisor reported that the cassava stems planted in April had sprouted well. A count taken on 30 May showed a survival rate of 92%. Weeding was required, and the Advisor recommended that the second weeding be done before the end of June. She noted that the rains had been adequate and no supplementary irrigation was needed.

*4.3 Fertilizer Distribution Programme*
Dr. Bello reported on the progress of the fertilizer distribution programme. As at 31 May 2024, the Union had distributed 1,240 bags of NPK 15:15:15 and 860 bags of urea to members. A total of 1,500 bags of NPK and 1,000 bags of urea had been procured from the Benue State Agricultural Supply Company. The balance of 260 bags of NPK and 140 bags of urea was in the Union's warehouse at Makurdi. The Advisor noted that the demand for fertilizer had been higher than anticipated, and she recommended that the Union consider procuring an additional 500 bags of NPK before the end of June. This matter was referred to the Finance Committee for advice.

*4.4 Training of Members on Climate-Smart Agriculture*
The Advisor reported that a one-day training on climate-smart agriculture had been held on 5 June 2024 at the Union's hall. Forty-two members attended. The training covered soil conservation, water management, and the use of drought-tolerant seed varieties. The Advisor noted that the turnout was good, but she expressed concern that only 18 of the 42 attendees were women. She recommended that future training sessions be scheduled on days when women were more likely to attend, and that the Union consider providing a small allowance for transport for women members from distant villages. The Executive took note of the recommendation and referred it to the Women's Committee.

*4.5 Seed Bank Status*
The Advisor reported that the Union's seed bank held the following as at 7 June 2024:
- Early maize (SAMMAZ 15): 320 kg
- Soybean (TGX 1448-2E): 210 kg
- Cowpea (SAMPEA 14): 150 kg
- Groundnut (SAMNUT 22): 95 kg

Mr. Terna reported that the distribution of improved cassava stems to the 120 registered participating farmers had been completed. A total of 96 hectares had been planted as at the end of August, against a target of 110 hectares for the first season. The shortfall was attributed to the late arrival of rains in some parts of the Gboko area, and to the fact that some farmers had diverted portions of their land to yam and maize.
